summary: Exports lift China's growth to 4.5% while shoppers stay cautious, Beijing proposes curbs on exporting solar know-how, and face-licensing for AI dramas disappoints.
body: China's economy grew 4.5% from July to September compared with a year earlier, a bit better than expected, but the gain came mostly from exports, which jumped 36% in September [^1]. At home, retail sales grew only 1.1% and property investment is down 20.6% this year, a sign that families hit by falling home values are still saving rather than spending [^1][^2]. A statistics official called weak domestic demand a "prominent problem" [^1].

On technology, the Commerce Ministry proposed export curbs on 12 solar manufacturing technologies, citing national security, as part of the same review that covers large AI models [^3]. Know-how for thin silicon wafers and next-generation perovskite and tandem solar cells would be banned from export; several advanced cell technologies would need approval [^3]. China dominates world solar manufacturing, so this would make it harder for the US, India and others to catch up. Comments close Nov. 15 [^3].

In daily life, a short-lived trend of "selling your face" to AI is fading. Since about May, platforms have let people license their likeness for AI-made short dramas, which officials say made up over 90% of the 430,000 such dramas released this year [^4]. Many users now report few requests and little pay, and Beijing's market regulator warned that criminals scrape selfies and voices to make AI avatars [^4].

reads.title: Western open-weight models still can't beat China
reads.summary: Why Chinese AI models that anyone can download, such as DeepSeek and Kimi, lead their Western rivals on cost and popularity, and what that means for who depends on whom.
